## Shipping release `v<VERSION>`

**Do not merge this PR directly.** The conductor keeps this branch (`release-prep/<REL_BRANCH>`) force-pushed on every push to `<REL_BRANCH>` — any commits made here (including a hand-merge) are silently overwritten on the next conductor run. Instead:

1. **Mark this PR ready-for-review** (out of draft) and approve it.
2. **Trigger the [ship-release workflow](../../actions/workflows/ship-release.yml)** via `workflow_dispatch` — pick `version` = `<VERSION>`, `rel_branch` = `<REL_BRANCH>`, and `mode` (default `semi-auto`, or `full-auto`, or `dry-run`).

In `semi-auto` and `full-auto` modes, ship-release then handles the annotated-tag creation, the paired `release-finalize/<REL_BRANCH>` master-side PR merge, and (in `full-auto` only) the `release-docs/<VERSION>` website PR merge. In `dry-run` mode (also the legacy `dry_run=true` input), ship-release stops after preflight + a dress-rehearsal package build — no tag, no PR merges, no downstream dispatches; the built artifacts land as a workflow-run artifact for eyeballing. See [RELEASE_PROCESS.md § Quick action 3 — Ship the release](../../docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md#3-ship-the-release) and the full runbook for the mode semantics, guardrails, and the recovery paths if any downstream step stalls.

`release-prep.yml` `gh workflow run`s **both** acceptance surfaces against this PR's tip on regenerations where the conductor actually force-pushed a diff (peter-evans no-op regens skip the dispatch; `release-prep-test/*` PRs skip too — see the `Trigger acceptance-*` step `if:` guards in `release-prep.yml`). These are `workflow_dispatch` runs, so **they do NOT appear in this PR's check list** — GitHub only surfaces `pull_request`-triggered runs there. Red runs are the early-warning signal — investigate and fix on `<REL_BRANCH>` before triggering ship-release. See [RELEASE_PROCESS.md § Phase 2 step 5](../../docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md#phase-2--branch-cut-and-pr-generation) for the dispatch mechanics + Phase 7c gate rationale.
